messages:
anya: Noticed a class of WS clients showing long pong latencies (~30s) after network blips. Console marks them as connected because resume works, but users report stalled streams and we keep billing tokens. Anyone seen similar?

matt: Yep. I instrumented a handful of traces: client lost for ~12s, reconnects, server accepts resume quickly but upstream app isn't actually sending events due to leftover backpressure. WS still counts as alive. Example: `recv_pong_delay=31s` then `resume_accept=true` but no events for 40s.

josh: Billing treats resume_accept as continuing session, we don't have a separate metric for end-to-end event liveness. We should differentiate 'transport alive' from 'application active'.

emily: On the console side we only color by connection state (open/closed). We can add a heatmap row for `last_event_age` and an alert if >15s for more than X% of sessions in a shard. That should make the user-visible stalls obvious.

sre-ops: If we add `last_event_age` telemetry, we can tie it to quota windows to avoid double-billing: if `last_event_age` > 20s and we accepted a resume within last 30s, mark those tokens as "suspended" for billing until events resume.

devex: Implementation options: 1) server-side probe: after resume, send a lightweight application-level ping frame and expect an application-level pong from handler within 5s. If handler doesn't respond, return 202 with `waiting_for_backend` (or close?). 2) Accept resume but emit `app_liveness=false` and suppress billing until we see an event. Option 1 is more immediate but could break clients expecting resume to be immediate.

matt: I prefer option 2 for rollout safety: accept resume, tag session `app_liveness=false`, emit telemetry and suppress billing. Add a short reconciliation window: if events arrive within 30s, retroactively mark billed tokens as billable; otherwise leave suppressed. We'll also store a `last_event_ts` per session in in-memory shard map.

josh: Need to be careful with retro-billing logic. Ledger code assumes events are billed when token consumption increments. If we suppress and later retro-bill, ensure idempotency and avoid double-counts. I'll add an atomic flag `billing_suppressed` on session state with a safe transition path.

emily: For console UX, we'll show a badge on sessions: `stalled (no events)` with tooltip explaining billing suppression. Also add a global toggle to disable suppression during canary tenants.

anya: Timeline: matt prototypes telemetry + `last_event_age` metric today, josh updates billing path to check `billing_suppressed` flag, emily updates dashboard and per-session hovercard. devex to craft client guidance about handling 409/202/ or annotation on resume.

matt: Quick pseudocode for probe I'm prototyping:
```
# on resume handler
session.last_event_ts = now()
if now() - session.last_event_ts > 15s:
  session.billing_suppressed = true
  emit(metric="app_liveness", tags={"session_id":id, "status":"stalled"})
else:
  session.billing_suppressed = false
```
I'll add tests to simulate delayed backend writes.

sre-ops: Alerting: fire if `stalled_sessions_pct` > 1% in eu shard for >5m. Also add an annotation in the console timeline when billing suppression toggles.

devex: Add note to the streaming SDKs: clients should treat resume 202/ack as "pending events" and display spinner until first application event arrives. We'll add short sample code for consuming first event.

anya: Agree on opt-in canary for 5% of tenants. deploy-bot, schedule a canary rollout when PRs are green.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for eng-platform/ws-app-liveness at 2026-03-23T02:00:00Z (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%).

matt: I'll land the telemetry and suppression flag behind a per-tenant feature flag. josh, I'll coordinate on ledger changes to avoid race.

josh: will do. Adding unit tests and a ledger integration test.

emily: I'll add the dashboard heatmap row and a per-session badge. Also linking a doc that explains billing suppression behavior.

anya: Thanks all. Follow-ups: write runbook for ops on how to un-suppress sessions if necessary, and add a console action to force-mark session active.

matt: ack.

sre-ops: ack.
